title: ModelBest Open-Sources MiniCPM-V 4.7, Its First MoE Multimodal Model, Running in 3GB on a Phone
source_used: Pandaily (article text read from the page's embedded data; the visible page was empty)
key_facts: ModelBest released MiniCPM-V 4.7, a new generation of its on-device multimodal (image-and-text) model family, in two sizes: 35B-A3B and 1B.
The 35B-A3B version is the first mixture-of-experts model in the MiniCPM-V series; weights, code and documentation are on the OpenBMB GitHub repository under the Apache-2.0 license.

ModelBest says the 35B-A3B model, which activates about 3 billion parameters per token, runs on an iPhone 17 Pro Max in about 3GB of memory at more than 13 tokens per second, thanks to a technique it calls lookahead expert scheduling (LES).
Benchmark scores reported by the team: 91.72 on MMBench, 91.2 on OCRBench and 90.21 on CMMLU; in Instruct mode it reaches a higher overall score than Qwen3.6 35B-A3B with shorter reasoning time.
The 1B version improves on MiniCPM-V 4.6 and, ModelBest says, leads Qwen3.5 0.8B on overall score and inference efficiency.
In hands-on tests published by QbitAI, the model handled chart reasoning and turned academic papers into Markdown with the phone offline.

It supports iOS, Android and HarmonyOS and has been adapted for chips from Intel, AMD, Arm, Rockchip and Houmo AI; ModelBest also open-sourced a fine-tuning recipe called Self-Replay Fine-Tuning (SRFT).
It follows MiniCPM-V 4.6 in May and the MiniCPM5-2B text model in September.
